# DocVQA Skill

## Visual Evidence Discipline
- Read the document carefully before answering.
- Prefer the smallest exact text span that answers the question.
- When several nearby strings look similar, choose the one whose surrounding labels or layout best match the question.
- For a question asking which entity, brand, service, or organization is advertised, shown, or mentioned, first decide whether the requested answer is the prominent identifying name or a longer corporate/legal description. When a short displayed name and a longer phrase containing legal, system, location, or descriptive wording are both visible, prefer the short identifying name unless the question explicitly asks for the full legal/registered name. If only the longer form is visible, return it rather than inventing a shorter variant, and do not append explanatory words from nearby text.

## Exact Answer Discipline
- For questions asking for a count (for example, "how many" or "number of"), return only the count token—the numeral or number word as printed—and omit the counted object or category. Do not append a noun phrase from a nearby caption, table header, or label when the count alone fully answers the question. When the question asks for a quantity or amount rather than a count of discrete objects, retain only a unit or measurement qualifier printed attached to the value, following the currency/unit selector rule below.
- Treat a currency, unit, or scale clause in the question ("in <currency>", "in thousands", or a parenthetical qualifier on the requested field) primarily as a selector for which field, column, or row to read. Return the value with exactly the characters printed with it—its digits, decimal point, grouping separators, and any symbol, currency mark, or unit printed attached. Do not prepend or append a symbol merely because the question names it. This does not license dropping parts of the printed token: keep any unit, code, or qualifier it contains intact and unsplit, and keep amount, date, and date-time spans as long as the printed entry requires. When one reading would attach decoration from the question and another from what is visibly printed beside the value, follow the printed form; do not upgrade the value to a more decorated version than the document shows.
- Copy names, numbers, and dates exactly from the document whenever possible. When the answer is a number, date, code, or measurement, this includes the printed punctuation and formatting: keep grouping/thousands separators, decimal marks, date separators (hyphen, slash, or dot), leading signs, and attached unit labels; do not drop, add, regroup, or normalize them, and do not reconstruct a partially legible or familiar-looking date, code, or figure from a standard format. When the value sits in a table cell or beside a label, keep it as one intact printed token rather than splicing characters from a neighboring number or merging two adjacent values into the answer.
- Treat the selected answer as one intact printed token. For a single value—such as a name-plus-code unit, a date or number range, a measurement, or an identifier—copy its characters and internal spacing exactly; do not adjust them for appearance or readability. Do not add whitespace that is not printed inside the token: if the joined parts show no visible gap, return them joined; if a visible gap exists, keep exactly that gap. Keep the token on one line and do not split it into pieces.
- Do not substitute a look-alike punctuation glyph. For a date or numeric range, return a plain hyphen when that is printed and an en or em dash when that is clearly printed; keep an apostrophe inside a token as an apostrophe rather than a quotation delimiter. The rule for ordinary straight ASCII quotation marks around a requested quoted title or slogan applies only to the marks delimiting that requested content; it does not authorize rewriting apostrophes, dashes, or other punctuation that is part of the printed value. When the separator glyph is not reliably distinguishable at the rendered size, choose the punctuation style used consistently elsewhere on the same page instead of defaulting to a typographic variant.
- First settle which characters are actually printed; these rules only preserve them. They do not change capitalization, add or remove units, currency symbols, decimals, or thousands separators, add quotation marks the document does not print, or shorten or lengthen the span. Full multi-word titles or headings, count tokens, and amount or date spans with their printed formatting keep their existing treatment.
- Prefer direct extraction over paraphrase.
- Determine whether the question asks for a labeled entry or for that entry's content. If it asks what a numbered heading, item, or field says, return only the content after the label, preserve its own words and capitalization, and omit the label and numbering. If it asks for the heading or label itself, or the label is part of the requested title, retain it. Do not shorten other answer types: answers that ask for a heading, title, agenda entry, sentence, or other full multi-word content require the complete requested entry as printed; when a requested name, phrase, or measurement requires more than a count token, keep the span as long as needed to be exact.
- Before finalizing, compare the answer against nearby alternatives and keep the best-supported exact span.
- When the requested answer is a title, slogan, or other content containing a quoted word, return the quoted portion verbatim in ordinary straight ASCII double quotation marks, not typographic curly quotes; quote style is formatting, not content. Do not add quotation marks merely because the question quotes a field name or label. If the answer span is not itself quoted in the document, return the plain span without decorative quotation marks.
